Knesset: Israel's parliament. It has 120 seats, so a government needs at least 61 to pass laws and survive.
coalition: A government formed by several parties that agree to work together because none won a majority alone.
impeachment: A formal process where a legislature charges a sitting leader with wrongdoing and can remove them from office.
house arrest: Being confined to your home by the authorities instead of being held in prison.
trilateral talks: Negotiations with three parties at the table, rather than just the two sides of a conflict.
Yellow Vests: A French protest movement, gilets jaunes, that began in 2018 over fuel taxes. It's named after the hi-vis vests every French driver must carry.
ANC: The African National Congress, Nelson Mandela's party. It has led South Africa since the first democratic elections in 1994.
apartheid: South Africa's system of legal racial segregation, from 1948 until the early 1990s.
MMP: Mixed-member proportional voting. Each party's share of seats closely matches its share of votes, so single-party majorities are rare.
Strait of Hormuz: The narrow channel between Iran and Oman. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes through it.
magnitude: How much energy an earthquake releases. The scale is logarithmic, so a 6 releases about 32 times more energy than a 5.
aftershocks: Smaller quakes that follow a big one, sometimes for days or weeks. A strong one can damage buildings already weakened.
Canary Islands: Spanish islands in the Atlantic, about 100 km off the coast of Morocco and Western Sahara.
midterms: US elections held halfway through a president's term, for all House seats and about a third of the Senate.
chief of staff: The president's most senior aide, who runs the White House and controls who gets the president's time.
press secretary: The White House spokesperson, who briefs reporters on the president's behalf, usually daily.
Uyghurs: A mostly Muslim, Turkic-speaking people from Xinjiang in western China, where rights groups document mass detention.
